the frequencies of pollen grains with extra and symmetrical nuclei increased in soybean anther culture and floral bud cold treatment, but only the number with typical extra nuclei was significant.

(1) the frequency of multinucleate grains increased with exposure time to both treatments; (2) the number of pollen with typical extra nuclei was significantly higher in both treatments; and (3) the number of atypical extra nuclei increased significantly after 28 days of exposure to both treatments.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the occurrence of typical extra nuclei is a response of soybean to culture and cold treatment, while the occurrence of atypical extra nuclei is a general response of soybean pollen grains to stress conditions.
the presence of typical and fragmented extra-nuclei is an indication of a possible androgenic response.
androgenesis in soybean is not an exclusive response of culture but also of cold treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the androgenic response in soybean pollen is not an exclusive response of anther culture, but it is also observed after floral buds cold treatment.

androgenic response is not only characterized by a multinuclear stage of pollen development, but also by the occurrence of atypical nuclei, which could be related with the programmed cell death of the pollen grain.
androgenic response and cold treatment of soybean floral buds increase symmetrical and extra-nucleated pollen grains.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the frequency of multinucleate and extra-nucleate pollen grains increased in response to culture of anthers and cold treatment of buds, and that these frequencies were not correlated with androgenesis in soybean.
the occurrence of multinucleate soybean pollen grains is not an exclusive response of androgenesis and it may be related to programmed cell death.
soybean pollen grains are able to respond to culture or cold treatment with the occurrence of extra nuclei, which may be related to androgenesis and/or cell death.
